messages.author: fbae97f3696b2723
messages.subject: spatial CAR model
parts:
Hi,  I am analysing some Poisson counts on a square grid where it might be useful to include spatial correlation among neighboring cells.  In particular I am interested in fitting the intrinsic conditional autoregressive or CAR model - similar to the car.normal() distribution available in WinBUGS.  

Anyway, I can fit the model in WinBUGS no problems but the chains converge slowly (but they do converge) so thought it might be useful to try implementing this in Nimble.

So following the example for creating a custom distribution function available on the website and a description of the conditional mean and variance of the CAR model from the GeoBUGS manual I put together the following code:

Briefly, adj is the 'adjacency matrix' (actually a vector) listing the ID's of the neighbours for all cells.  offset is a vector of positions listing the neighbours for each cell such that adj[(offset[i]+1):offset[i+1]] are the neighbours for cell i.  numN is a vector giving the number of neighbors for each cell and tau is the precision parameter.

For the 'weights' I assume that all neighbours of a cell have a weight of 1 and 0 otherwise.

The problem is I can't get the following code to work.   In fact compileNimble(dcar.normal) fails so I obviously have some misunderstanding of nimbleFunction syntax.

I'd be grateful for any help.

thanks
Dave


dcar.normal<- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1), adj=integer(1), offset=integer(1), numN=integer(1),
                 tau=double(0), log = logical(0, default = 0)) {
    returnType(double(1))
    n<- dim(x)[1]
    z<- numeric(n, init=FALSE)
    for(i in 1:n){
      x.adj<- adj[(offset[i]+1):offset[i+1]]
      mu<- mean(x[x.adj])
      V<- 1/tau
      sigmaS<- sqrt(V/numN[i])
      z[i]<- dnorm(x[i], mu, sigmaS)
    }
    return(z)
  })

rcar.normal<- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(n=integer(), adj=integer(1), off=integer(1), numN=integer(1),
                 tau=double(0)) {
    returnType(double(1))
    nregions<- dim(num)[1] 
    V<- 1/tau
    sigmaS<- sqrt(V/numN)
    # not sure the following is correct
    return(rnorm(nregions, 0, sigmaS))
    })

registerDistributions(list(
  dcar.normal = list(
    BUGSdist = "dcar.normal(adj, offset, numN, tau)",
    discrete = FALSE,
    range = c(-Inf, Inf),
    types = c('value = double(1)', 'adj = integer(1)', 'offset = integer(1)',
              'numN=integer(1)','tau=double(0)')
  )))

For the 'weights' I assume that all neighbours of a cell have a weight of 1 and 0 otherwise.

The problem is I can't get the following code to work.   In fact compileNimble(dcar.normal) fails so I obviously have some misunderstanding of nimbleFunction syntax.

I'd be grateful for any help.

thanks
Dave


dcar.normal<- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1), adj=integer(1), offset=integer(1), numN=integer(1),
                 tau=double(0), log = logical(0, default = 0)) {
    returnType(double(1))

A “d” function should always return a scalar (“returnType(double(0))”). NIMBLE will treat a node declared to follow dcar.normal as a single node, with a single log probability density value associated with it.

n<- dim(x)[1]
    z<- numeric(n, init=FALSE)
    for(i in 1:n){
      x.adj<- adj[(offset[i]+1):offset[i+1]]
      mu<- mean(x[x.adj])
Unfortunately NIMBLE won’t compile arbitrary indexing like “x[x.adj]” yet.  It will handle that in the future.  For now you will have to write a for loop to accomplish what you want.

V<- 1/tau
      sigmaS<- sqrt(V/numN[i])
      z[i]<- dnorm(x[i], mu, sigmaS)

Because a “d” function should return a scalar, you’ll have to add up the dnorm values that you are currently putting in a vector.  Also, NIMBLE will call a “d” function with “log = TRUE”, so you must support that.  I suggest using dnorm(x[i], mu, sigmaS, log = TRUE), adding up results from that for each i.  Then use something like

if(log) return(sum_of_z)
else return(exp(sum_of_z))

}
    return(z)
  })




rcar.normal<- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(n=integer(), adj=integer(1), off=integer(1), numN=integer(1),
                 tau=double(0)) {
    returnType(double(1))
    nregions<- dim(num)[1] 
    V<- 1/tau
    sigmaS<- sqrt(V/numN)
    # not sure the following is correct
    return(rnorm(nregions, 0, sigmaS))

NIMBLE won’t compile a vectorized call to rnorm.  That is something else that will work in the future.  For now you will have to do something like

result <- numeric(nregions)
for(i in 1:nregions) result[i] <- rnorm(1, 0, sigmaS)
return(result)

})

registerDistributions(list(
  dcar.normal = list(
    BUGSdist = "dcar.normal(adj, offset, numN, tau)",
    discrete = FALSE,
    range = c(-Inf, Inf),
    types = c('value = double(1)', 'adj = integer(1)', 'offset = integer(1)',
              'numN=integer(1)','tau=double(0)')
  )))

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: spatial CAR model
parts:
Hi Dave, just a note of caution here: it doesn't look to me that your
specification correctly specifies the joint distribution for all the
components. The sum of the log densities for the individual components
is not the density for the components jointly because of the
dependence between the components.

We're hoping to implement a CAR model in the somewhat near future. The
difficulty is that specifying the distribution of each component in a
spatial CAR in a univariate fashion does not give a directed acyclic
graph. We can write down the density for all the components jointly
(which has a sparse precision matrix), but then if one does univariate
sampling, one is recomputing the density for all the components every
time a single one is updated, which is inefficient.

-chris
